chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام), who said:
The deeds are presented to the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله), the deeds of the servants, every morning, both their righteous ones and their wicked ones. So beware of them.
And this is the saying of Allah, the Exalted: “Work, and Allah will see your deeds, and His Messenger.”

key_terms.الْأَعْمَالُ: deeds or actions performed by people
key_terms.الْعِبَادِ: the servants, meaning human beings as servants of Allah
key_terms.رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah, Muḥammad (صلى الله عليه وآله)
key_terms.فَاحْذَرُوهَا: so beware of them; a warning regarding one’s actions
key_terms.فَسَيَرَى اللَّهُ عَمَلَكُمْ وَرَسُولُهُ: Allah and His Messenger will see your deeds

ai.seo_question: Are people’s deeds presented to the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله)?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the deeds of the servants are presented every morning to the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله), including both righteous and sinful deeds. It cites the Qur’anic statement about Allah and His Messenger seeing human deeds, indicating a divinely authorized awareness tied to moral accountability. The report serves as a warning to remain cautious regarding one’s actions.
